headline: Error Hunter: Find and Fix Grammar Errors
problemStatement: Proofreading improves when learners have to identify a problem, propose a correction, and explain what changed. Error Hunter gives students a paragraph with hidden grammar errors, then lets them hunt on their phones before the class reviews the fixes one by one.
outcomes: Practice spotting grammar errors in connected writing rather than isolated sentences.
Build editing confidence by making a correction and checking it against a clear answer key.
Discuss why an error is wrong and how to repair it.
howItWorks: Choose a topic and difficulty to generate a paragraph with a set number of mistakes.
Students mark the words they believe contain errors and submit corrections on their phones during a timed race.
Accurate hunts earn points, with a speed bonus for students who find the errors; an empty or inaccurate hunt does not get a speed bonus.
The round can end when everyone has submitted. During review, the teacher steps through the paragraph with each error struck through, its fix, its type, and the number of hunters who found it.
teacherUseCases: Use a short hunt before a writing task to remind students to check target grammar in their own paragraphs.
Pause at each revealed correction and ask learners to say the corrected sentence or explain the grammar rule.

faq.q: Can students submit a correction from their phone?
faq.a: Yes. Students select the error words and provide corrections through their phone input. The teacher screen collects the race results for review.

faq.q: Does an empty answer earn the speed bonus?
faq.a: No. The speed bonus is available only for an accurate hunt, which requires students to find and correct the errors.

faq.q: How does the answer reveal work?
faq.a: The teacher can reveal errors one at a time or show them all. Each correction is visible in the original paragraph with the error struck through.
The race ends once all active students have submitted. The class can move directly to the step-through reveal and discuss which errors were easiest to miss.
